turns.message: Could you make the frame rate steadier without touching my resolution or anti-aliasing? Also tell me what ambient occlusion does. Remember that I put seeing enemies ahead of graphics quality.
turns.reply: To stabilize your frame rate while prioritizing visibility over aesthetics, I recommend the following adjustments. These focus on reducing GPU overhead from heavy visual effects like shadows, particles, and depth mapping. Regarding your question: **Ambient Occlusion** simulates how light is blocked by objects. It adds soft shadows in crevices and where two surfaces meet (like the corner of a wall). While it makes the world look more grounded and realistic, it is a purely aesthetic feature and can be disabled to save resources without affecting your ability to see enemies. Selected adjustments: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 **Main Trade-off:** These changes will significantly reduce the visual fidelity of the game (making textures, shadows, and particles look less 'polished') in exchange for a more consistent and higher frame rate. Since you prioritized seeing enemies over graphics, these are the most effective changes to make. **Uncertainty:** The exact impact on your frame rate depends heavily on your specific hardware; some settings (like Global Shadow Quality) may have a larger impact on some GPUs than others.

turns.message: Are those little dark creases around corners from ambient occlusion or the same shadows that players cast? Show me where to inspect ambient occlusion without changing anything.
turns.reply: Ambient occlusion adds shading near contacts and in crevices, helping surfaces look less flat. Dynamic Shadows determines which light sources make moving objects cast shadows. Player shadows can be a visibility cue indoors, while ambient occlusion mainly adds depth and rendering work.
